30 landmark tests: how stable is a face score?

Does eye-line alignment keep a symmetry measurement stable when an image rotates, and what happens when one jaw point moves?

By AI Rate FaceFormula sensitivity experimentCalculated September 8, 2026

What this experiment shows

The combined score spans 81–87 in these 30 configurations. Compare rows with the same jaw shift to isolate rotation; compare rows with the same rotation to isolate the moved point. The combined score also includes photo presentation.

Inputs and method

We use one hand-authored 478-position coordinate fixture in a 900 × 900 image. We combine five in-plane rotations (−12°, −6°, 0°, 6°, 12°) with six left-jaw shifts (0 to 18 pixels). Brightness, contrast and sharpness inputs stay fixed. All 30 configurations run through the production geometry and overall-score functions. These are coordinate tests, not 30 photographs.

Calculation version: ARF calculation experiments 1.0. Engine: ARF Local Geometry v3.0.

How to use this when reading your result

Repeatability has two parts: identical inputs should give identical calculations, while changed inputs can give changed results. Alignment can correct an image-plane rotation, but it cannot recover hidden geometry from a head turn or determine whether a landmark shift came from expression, camera perspective or detection error.

Test your photo consistency →

What this experiment cannot tell you

The fixture has hand-set coordinates only for the landmarks needed by the calculations; unused coordinates are at the centre. It is not an anatomically validated face. No image decoding or MediaPipe inference is tested, so this experiment does not establish photo-to-photo reliability or demographic accuracy.

Sources and calculation choices

  • MediaPipe Face Landmarker documentation — Google AI Edge. Documents the model and its 478 estimated landmarks. Our scores, shape profiles and style suggestions are our own calculations, not MediaPipe outputs. A landmark detector is not an attractiveness model and does not validate our scoring weights.
